prediction_tested: R127 predicted that rewriting the slider episode as drag -> read #val -> correct by residual would converge. This tests it.

outcomes.note: goal regex did not match; NOT a capability failure, excluded from the honest denominator

what_converged: both successes landed the value EXACTLY on the target integer. One needed a single correction, the other needed four.
what_did_not: 14->10, 3->2, 106->109. These are small-integer residuals that four corrections did not close. A mouse drag moves in pixel quanta; at the observed track widths some integer values are not reachable by dragging alone.
the_precise_law: a closed correction loop removes COARSE calibration error and cannot remove error finer than the resolution of the actuator. Prediction from R127 was directionally right (0 -> 2) and quantitatively wrong (not 6/6).
why_this_matters_for_computer_use_as_a_w: the 2026 ComponentBench finding is that continuous calibration error is the single largest error class (20.2%) and is 'resistant to added reasoning'. This measurement localises WHY: the residual is below the action resolution, so more reasoning cannot fix it and more corrections cannot either.
the remedy is not a better policy. It is a finer actuator: keyboard arrow keys step a slider by exactly one unit where a drag cannot.
this is a testable next step with a known-mechanism answer rather than a guess.

the_answer_to_the_users_recurring_questi.instant_learning_solves: any task whose correctness can be OBSERVED and whose error can be CORRECTED at a scale larger than the actuator's resolution
the_answer_to_the_users_recurring_questi.instant_learning_does_not_solve: targets finer than the actuator can express, and tasks where the result cannot be observed before the episode is scored
the_answer_to_the_users_recurring_questi.measured_evidence_across_this_session: menu 8/8 and 9/10 (relations, observable, correctable); drag 6/6 (geometric relation, observable at submit); slider 0/6 open-loop and 2/5 measured closed-loop (continuous, residual below actuator resolution)
